instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Toss the 1 1/2 cups panko with 2 tbsp of the olive oil on a large rimmed baking sheet and spread it out in an even layer.
Toast the panko in the oven for 4 to 6 minutes, stirring halfway, until it's light golden. Keep an eye on it near the end. It goes from golden to burnt quickly.
Tip the panko into a wide shallow bowl and stir in the 1/4 cup parmesan, the 2 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper. Turn the oven up to 425°F.
Brush the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over the same baking sheet.
Pat the 1.25 lb cod dry with paper towels and cut it into strips about 3/4 inch wide and 4 inches long.
In another bowl, whisk the egg with 1 tbsp of the mayonnaise, the 2 tbsp flour and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper until it's smooth.
Put the fish in the egg mix and turn it gently with a spatula to coat every strip. Work straight away. If the coated fish sits around it turns watery.

Lift the strips out one at a time with tongs and lay them in the panko. Spoon crumbs over the top and press them on with your fingers. Set each one on the oiled baking sheet with a little space around it.

Bake for 12 to 14 minutes, until the crumbs are deep golden and crisp. You're cooking it to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one of the thickest sticks. No thermometer? Break one open: it's done when the fish is white all the way through and flakes apart.
While they bake, finely chop the 2 dill pickles. Stir them into the remaining 1/2 cup mayonnaise with the juice of half the lemon. Taste the tartar sauce, and add a pinch of salt if it's flat.
Cut the rest of the lemon into wedges.
Serve the fish sticks hot with the tartar sauce and the lemon wedges.
method_notes: All three cut firm white fish into strips, coat them in seasoned panko and bake them hot on a sheet, and the two most detailed ones toast the panko in oil first so it browns before the fish overcooks. RecipeTin Eats (the most rated) toasts plain panko at 350°F, mixes in parmesan and paprika, uses a single batter of egg, mayonnaise and flour instead of separate flour and egg dips, and bakes the strips at 425°F for 13 minutes. Carlsbad Cravings adds cornmeal and a big dried herb mix and bakes on a rack at 450°F; Killing Thyme uses a flour, egg and Old Bay panko line and bakes at 425°F to 140 to 145°F. This one follows RecipeTin Eats and makes a quick tartar sauce from mayonnaise, pickles and lemon, the dip all three serve.
